title: Sowing and planting A sound start
brief: Direct sowing in a row in open soil; module seedlings on the greenhouse bench; planting a hardened-off lettuce plug into open garden soil.
setting: The two outer photographs are on the lawn side of the home garden bed, looking towards the greenhouses. The middle photograph is inside on the timber staging.

outdoor_generation.prompt:
Make a matched outdoor PAIR of true-to-life editorial photographs for John Lennon's British gardening book. Output one 2:1 wide diptych: exactly TWO distinct square pictures, side by side, edge to edge; hard cut at exact midpoint; no divider, margins, graphic overlays or lettering. These are two OUTDOOR replacement photographs. A separate existing indoor seed-tray picture will go between them in the book after cropping. Do not illustrate that indoor step. Work on soil continuous with the earth, in John's actual BACK GARDEN, in the open air. References 1 and 2 are real photos of his garden. Reference 1 sets the view facing toward the greenhouses, but here replace the cardboard with fine seedbed soil; reference 2 shows the actual slim ground-level bed perimeter, irregular green lawn beside it, and low height of the established bed. Frame toward the greenhouses, exclude the old glazed porch in reference 2 entirely. Reference 3 is for John's hands and oatmeal knit only. Reference 4 shows the previous nursery stage for continuity of the Little Gem lettuce and hand scale only. There are NO plant pots, no troughs or containers, no bench, no slats, no nursery trays, and no greenhouse framing OVERHEAD, in either of these outdoor shots. Soil fills the foreground and extends generously beyond the hand to show working at ground level in a real long, full-size open garden bed. Show a distinct, believable strip of real adjacent lawn in both views. A little of the low edging or the distant brick base of John's freestanding greenhouse may be glimpsed at upper edge, behind the lawn, if framing allows. Never put a large box or raised boards around the soil.

LEFT: DIRECT SOWING OUTDOORS. A close documentary camera looks diagonally DOWN the length of the garden bed, at kneeling height. Long shallow narrow continuous seed drill in fine, naturally damp garden tilth runs diagonally from near left toward upper right across the picture. It is visibly a straight row several hand-lengths long, with fine loose crumbs, small weathered particles, no deep trench. John's right hand enters frame at the side, thumb and one forefinger pinching and sowing tiny buff-brown ridged carrot seeds THINLY in the bottom of this groove (just several natural seeds, irregular but thinly spaced, 2–3mm, slimmer and smaller than rice, none enlarged or hanging in the air). Wrist of flecked oatmeal gardening jumper. Frame both the hand and enough row for the viewer to see direct sowing seed into the ground at a glance. No seedlings here. Soft cool spring outdoor light.

RIGHT: PLANTING A HARDENED-OFF LETTUCE MODULE INTO THE OUTDOOR BED weeks later. Same garden, low-camera oblique close shot from lawn side. Show one of John's bare mature hands supporting the sides of a SMALL moist square-tapered ROOT PLUG while easing its bottom halfway into a snug planting hole made in the soil of the big OUTDOOR garden bed. The top half of the cohesive dark root ball and two or three fine pale roots on it still visible; small realistic lettuce with 3–5 soft, muted young leaves, crown upright. Other hand on ground gently drawing loose earth towards plug; anatomically credible relaxed hands, fingers holding soil not stem. Navy knitted sleeve as a subtle different day. A single earlier planted lettuce farther down the bed about one hand span away can establish row direction. Avoid mature heads, bare dangling roots, seed trays and lined-up rows of uniformly perfect plants. Slightly brighter spring light. The bare ground and rough grass immediately beyond the bed are visible in this picture as well.

Pair of properly focused photoreal close-up photographs in natural Cornish daylight for a practical manual. Understated, ordinary gardening, no staged tool displays. Accurate anatomy (at most two hands per frame); close on actions, no head, torso or faces. At 48 mm printed width still readable. Aim a little wider than the indoor reference so we can tell instantly that these jobs are OUTSIDE in earth. Main hand and central action must sit well inside each square.

references.role: Module-raised lettuce and hands for visual continuity

photographs.role: Original greenhouse module tray photograph retained exactly.
